title: A node of the specification
$comment: The one description of a node's structure, its metadata included. The file schema refers to it and never restates it, and a node refers to itself for the nodes under it. Each kind adds its own fields through a condition on kind, so an error names the field that is wrong rather than every kind the node is not. A field nobody declared is refused: it would be a field nobody remembers the purpose of, and admitting one lets them accumulate.

node.$comment: The fields and the conditions on `kind` shared by every node. Each schema that refers to this one says whether a sid and a title are required or refused, and whether an undeclared field is refused.

allOf.$comment: A section: a container of rules, whose text states what it is responsible for and requires nothing. It may name owners of its own, any of whom approves every node within it. Its status is built from the nodes under it and approved by nobody.
One rule. A rule may describe a list.

A rule set out as a table (s-5fewsp22mmdz7y6). It has a title, a text and a reason, as a TextRule has; it also names its table's columns, and holds the table's rows, grouped under headings. Each cell holds text or a node; a node in a cell has no title of its own, since its column and its row name it. `sheriff validate` checks what the schema cannot: that the column keys are distinct, that every row has a cell for each column and for no other, and that each cell holds what its column says.

columns.$comment: The table's columns, in the order in which they are read.

key.$comment: The name by which a row's cells refer to the column.

heading.$comment: The column's heading as the table shows it.

holds.$comment: What each cell of the column holds: a node, or text that is part of the wording of the TableRule.

groups.$comment: The table's rows in groups, in the order in which they are read. A table whose rows are not grouped holds one group, whose heading is null.

cellNode.$comment: A node in a cell of a TableRule: an ordinary node except that it has no title of its own, since its column and its row name it.

kind.$comment: A term's title is the term it defines; a TableRule is a rule set out as a table. An extension of the schema adds kinds of its own, such as a domain's header, which the Domains extension adds, and the RecordType, which the RecordType extension adds (s-xzcw3hv4hmxz7h7).

title.$comment: What the node is called where it is shown in a few words — in a link, in an index, in the map: a term's title is the term it defines, a RecordType's the RecordType's name.

text.$comment: What must hold; for a section or a header, what it is responsible for.

reason.$comment: Why the requirement in text must hold; not part of it.

examples.$comment: Examples of what the text states, each a typical case of applying the node and, where that helps, the mistake closest to that case (s-pqemhjzvxtw4byc). Part of the node's wording, though an example imposes no requirement.

refs.$comment: A link is declared once: a second copy of it says nothing the first does not, and the reindex would build it twice into the other node's list.

archived.$comment: Only on a node in the archive: when and why it was removed, and the sid of the node that replaces it, if one does. validate requires it there and refuses it anywhere else, which the schema cannot tell apart.

children.$comment: The nodes under this one, in the order in which they are read. Nesting alone gives the tree: there is no parent field and no order field, so no such field can contradict where the node actually is.

location.$comment: A location: the part the node is in followed by its place there, e.g. contracts/4.1, or the domain's name alone for the header of a domain. Computed by the reindex from where the node is and never written by hand; nothing refers to it.

sid.$comment: A node's permanent identifier: s- and fifteen characters drawn at random from lowercase letters and digits without 0, o, 1, l and i, which are read for one another. Given once and never changed, and held by every reference to the node.

status.$comment: approved: one of the node's owners approved its present wording; draft otherwise. A section's and a domain's header's status is built by the reindex from the nodes under it.

owners.$comment: The owners of a domain or a section, each named by an email, with equal rights; absent where the owners above hold.

date.$comment: A day as ISO 8601 writes it, the year first, so that dates read the same in every language and sort as text.

ref.$comment: A link as the node holds it, read from this node's end. An entry naming to is one the node makes, written by hand; an entry naming from points at the node, is built by the reindex and is never written by hand. An entry names exactly one of the two.

type.$comment: What the link states about the two nodes it binds, chosen from a closed list so that every check knows what each link means. An extension of the schema adds types of its own, such as consumes, which the Domains extension adds (s-xzcw3hv4hmxz7h7).

ratio.$comment: Required on a term-relation and refused on every other link: a link between rules binds one node to one, so a ratio on it would state a multiplicity nobody could mean.

The multiplicity at each end of a term-relation in UML notation, the end at the node that holds the entry comes first (s-bckzdwd35d2nefa): a whole number, or a range of whole numbers whose upper bound may be *, meaning no upper bound. Both ends are given, because one end alone cannot say whether the other may be absent: 1:0..1 and 1:1 differ in exactly that respect.

list.$comment: A list a rule describes — a set of states, the members of a category, the routes of a table — held as members rather than as prose, because a machine compares it with the declaration in the code or in a schema that carries it. declaredIn names that declaration and is absent until the code exists: the rule is written first and implemented second.

of.$comment: What the list is of, in one line, so that it says which declaration is its counterpart.

members.$comment: Each member on its own, so that a machine can compare them with the declaration that holds them: a primitive value, or an object whose property the list names holds its value and whose other properties state what holds of it.

property.$comment: Where a member is an object: the property each such member holds its value under.

declaration.$comment: In code, the name of the declaration; in a schema, a JSON pointer to the enum, which reaches one standing inside another as well.

jsonSchema.$comment: The place in a JSON Schema whose values the list states: the file, and a JSON pointer within it.

valueList.$comment: The symbol in code that declares the list's values: the file, and the name of the symbol.

meta.$comment: What accumulates around a node without being part of its wording: what was decided about it, the code and tests bound to it, comments and the work deferred on it. Changing it does not change the node's status. It is kept in the node, so that whoever reads a node sees it whole in one place.

items.$comment: What was settled about the node: a problem, and the ruling on it. textual: the ruling changed the node's wording; procedural: it changed none.

code.$comment: The code bound to the node: each file that holds a symbol whose SpecTag names the node. sheriff reindex writes the list from the SpecTags (s-ztseyetus7np6br), and sheriff binding compares the list with the one that the SpecTags produce (s-t383grkn3q68dpf).

tests.$comment: The tests carrying the node's SpecTag, each as its file and name; compared with the tests by binding.

items.$comment: A remark on the node: when, whose and what. A comment of type problem is an open problem, not yet a decision or a todo, and leaves the list once it is settled. A comment opening with TODO is refused: deferred work is a todos item, and one left in a comment is missed by everything that collects what waits.

A task or an idea put off until later, kept on the node it concerns: when it was put off, whose word it is, and what is to be done. An item is removed once it is done, git keeping its history and a ruling it led to going to the node's decisions.

columnKey.$comment: The key of a column of a TableRule: an identifier in camelCase.

row.$comment: A row of a TableRule: its cells, each under the key of its column.

cell.$comment: A cell of a TableRule: text that is part of the wording of the TableRule, or a node of its own.
